clue.text: Right piece, wrong method

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order, so they get rearranged

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A complaint that the correct part has been fitted using the wrong technique.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions for making something, so a method or formula for achieving a result.

clue.text: Ferry with two paddles docked

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to paddle is to row, and two of them gives the word twice

explanation.surface: A boat fitted with a pair of oars, tied up at the quay.
explanation.walkthrough: Each ROW loses its last letter, leaving RO-RO, short for roll-on roll-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off vessel that vehicles drive on and off, a common type of car ferry.

clue.text: Farm worker that hurts children with pinches

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between fingers, so one piece is gripped inside another

blocks.note: CH is a common abbreviation for children
the exclamation someone makes when something hurts
and means together with

explanation.surface: A cruel labourer who pinches the local kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' reads as the cruelty in the surface, but it tells you one piece is squeezed inside another; 'that hurts' is the cry itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowhand is a person employed to look after cattle, a kind of hired labourer on a ranch or farm.

clue.text: President stable after second popper

indicators.note: placing one item after another fixes the order in which the parts are joined

blocks.note: PRES is a standard abbreviation for president
S is the abbreviation for second
a stud is a stable or establishment where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: A leader whose horses are kept in the yard behind a second-in-command's.
explanation.walkthrough: A popper is the British word for a press stud, the two-part snap fastener on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Popper is a British name for the snap fastener on clothes, which pops open when pulled.

clue.text: Vice rings close to you? Say no more

indicators.note: something that rings another encircles it, so it goes round the outside
'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'you'

blocks.note: a vice is a tool that clamps work in place
the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A wicked habit that circles back to you, so you had better keep quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' selects the last letter of 'you'; the bench tool goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is an idiom meaning to stop talking abruptly, which is what the order to say no more demands.

clue.text: Charlie's best friend left where Americans live

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Americans live in the US

explanation.surface: A friend of someone called Charlie departed for America.
explanation.definitionFit: Linus van Pelt is Charlie Brown's closest friend in the Peanuts comic strip.

clue.text: Cocktail one can spoil, layering parts from the bottom

indicators.note: building the layers upward from the base means the last-named part sits on top of this down entry

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
a tin is a can
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A warning that one can of something could ruin a carefully layered drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are stacked from the base of this down entry upward in clue order, so the last-named sits at the top and the first-named at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a classic cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Long bug, thin leaf

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
to needle someone is to bug or irritate them

explanation.surface: A description of an insect: a long bug resembling a slender leaf, like a stick insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Conifers like the pine have narrow needle-shaped foliage, so a pine needle is a slender leaf.

clue.text: Bullied little sibling with book bolted

blocks.note: bro is a short form of brother
W is an abbreviation for with
B is an abbreviation for book
to bolt food is to eat it quickly

explanation.surface: A younger brother pushed around and made to swallow a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened form rather than a younger child.
explanation.definitionFit: Browbeaten means intimidated with threats or harsh words, which is what being bullied involves.

clue.text: Bill allowed nine wayward sons a little sport

indicators.note: wayward things stray from their proper course, so these letters wander out of order

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
let means allowed
taken as written, as anagram fodder
S is an abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father named Bill lets his nine unruly boys play a bit of sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: table tennis is a miniature version of tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis is tennis shrunk to a tabletop, so it is a small-scale version of that sport.

clue.text: Crossbar split goalie's head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to split, slang for leaving in a hurry, is to run
the opening letter of goalie

explanation.surface: A football goal frame broken by a keeper's header.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossbar' and 'goalie' paint a football scene, but the crossbar here is on a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is one of the horizontal bars of a ladder or chair, a crosspiece.

clue.text: Seaside town without a bean - it's struggling

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: sans is French for without, used in English
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A beach resort that has gone broke and is having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: San Sebastián is a resort city on the Basque coast of Spain, famous for its beach.

clue.text: 4 running shelter not happy

blocks.note: 4-across is CLAM UP, read here as an instruction: the word CLAM written upward in this down entry
a machine that is running is on
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: A sheltered spot that leaves someone unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does double duty: the answer to 4 is CLAM UP, and in a down clue 'up' tells you to write CLAM bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a dissatisfied, discontented person; mal- (bad) plus content (pleased) captures being displeased.

clue.text: Criminal gang appeal

blocks.note: a band is a group or gang
IT means sex appeal, as in the old phrase 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A criminal mob launching a legal challenge against a conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw or robber, a type of lawbreaker.

clue.text: A floating hazard in river one tries to pass

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
a sea mine floats as a hazard to shipping
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A boat crew trying to steer past a drifting danger in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a boat dodging an obstacle, but passing means getting through a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An examinee is a candidate sitting a test, someone trying to pass the exam.

clue.text: Heartless pal during year out circulated impersonal email

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle of the word is taken out
things circulated are passed around and mixed up, so these letters are rearranged
during places one piece within the span of the other

blocks.note: the word pal minus its middle letter
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A friend away for a gap year sent round a cold, impersonal message.
explanation.definitionFit: An autoreply is an automatically generated response such as an out-of-office message, sent without personal input.

clue.text: Green building, perimeter walls half painted

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the rest being dropped
to wall something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the edge is the perimeter
painted means coloured

explanation.surface: A building painted green, its outer walls only half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the paint colour but means environmentally friendly; only the first half of the synonym for painted is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecolodge is environmentally friendly tourist accommodation, and green means eco-friendly.

clue.text: Couple making king new centre of family tree

indicators.note: a new centre means the middle letter is swapped out for the royal symbol

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
a lineage is a line of descent, as charted on a family tree

explanation.surface: A marriage that puts a monarch at the heart of the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle E of LINEAGE is replaced by K.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple, as a mechanical connector joining two parts, is a linkage; linkage means coupling.

clue.text: Drink little and often - advice applied regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a tip is a piece of advice
the second, fourth and sixth letters of applied

explanation.surface: Health advice on drinking: small amounts, frequently, applied consistently.
explanation.definitionFit: To tipple is to drink alcohol habitually in small quantities, the steady sipping of a regular drinker.

clue.text: Spin dry tops for instance, each plain

indicators.note: tops are the uppermost parts, so in a down clue the first letters of the following words are taken

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is spin
to air laundry is to dry it
the first letters of instance and each

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: spin, then dry the tops, each one flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is laundry instructions; 'plain' is a noun, a broad flat stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast area of flat grassland in North America, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Very old article on Iran, say, soon after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns everything over, so the letters gathered so far are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written
e.g., for example, is what say means
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A political report on a long-lived regime: Iran shortly after its revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagenarian is someone aged between ninety and ninety-nine, certainly elderly.

clue.text: With plenty of spaces, parking twice in fun?

indicators.note: in means the preceding pieces are set inside the next word

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, and twice doubles it
gay in its older sense of merry or full of fun

explanation.surface: A car park with lots of empty bays, where parking twice might be fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaces' looks like parking bays, but it means gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Gappy describes something full of gaps or holes, so having many empty spaces.

clue.text: Award for Dune to hold and cherish alongside Oscar

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side in order

blocks.note: to hug is to hold someone close with affection
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Dune the film, an award contender sitting alongside its Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' tempts as a film award, given Dune's movies, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hugo is the major science-fiction literary prize, and Frank Herbert's novel Dune won it in 1966.

clue.text: Letter expected answer

blocks.note: 'I bet' means I expected it, as in 'I bet you'd say that'
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A letter received that contained the reply one had anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Job role that's doubtful after childbirth

blocks.note: a post is a job
a part is a role in a play
um is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: A new mother unsure about returning to her job after having a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Postpartum is the medical term for the period following delivery of a baby.

clue.text: Colouring by hand drawn by the old you

blocks.note: a drawn game is tied
ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Colouring something in by hand, as you used to draw it in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests sketching, but it is the sporting sense of a match ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dye is a hand method of dyeing fabric by knotting it so the colour takes in patterns.

clue.text: Music from Louisiana ends in jazz medley, 20s style

indicators.note: the ends of words are their final letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the final letters of jazz and medley
art deco was the design style of the 1920s

explanation.surface: A description of a Louisiana band finishing with a jazz medley in Roaring Twenties style.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is the accordion-led dance music of the Creole people of southwest Louisiana.
